ex:
// A thirteenth-century Persian rhythm called Khafif-e-ramal.

note("c3").euclidRot(3,5,2)

note("c3").euclid(3,7)

// Another Ruchenitza Bulgarian folk-dance rhythm.

// The Aksak rhythm of Turkey.
note("c3").euclid(4,9)

note("c3").euclid(4,11)

note("c3").euclid(5,6)

// The Nawakhat pattern, another popular Arab rhythm.
note("c3").euclid(5,7)

// A popular Arab rhythm called Agsag-Samai.
note("c3").euclid(5,9)

note("c3").euclid(5,11)

note("c3").euclid(7,8)

name: absoluteOrientationAlpha
desc: The device's absolute orientation alpha value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: absoluteOrientationBeta
desc: The device's absolute orientation beta value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: absoluteOrientationGamma
desc: The device's absolute orientation gamma value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: accelerate
desc: A pattern of numbers that speed up (or slow down) samples while they play. Currently only supported by osc / superdirt.

name: accelerationX
desc: The accelerometer's x-axis value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: accelerationY
desc: The accelerometer's y-axis value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: accelerationZ
desc: The accelerometer's z-axis value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: add
desc: Assumes a pattern of numbers. Adds the given number to each item in the pattern.

name: addVoicings
desc: Adds a new custom voicing dictionary.

name: adsr
desc: ADSR envelope: Combination of Attack, Decay, Sustain, and Release.

name: aliasBank
desc: Register an alias for a bank of sounds. Optionally accepts a single argument map of bank aliases. Optionally accepts a single argument string of a path to a JSON file containing bank aliases.

params.name: alias
params.desc: The alias to use for the bank

name: almostAlways
desc: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0.9, fn)

name: almostNever
desc: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0.1, fn)

name: always
desc: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(1, fn) (always calls fn)

name: amp
desc: Like gain, but linear.

name: anchor
desc: The top note to align the voicing to. Defaults to c5

params.name: anchorNote
params.desc: the note to align the voicings to

name: apply
desc: Like layer, but with a single function:

name: arp
desc: Selects indices in in stacked notes.

name: arpWith
desc: Selects indices in in stacked notes.

name: arrange
desc: Allows to arrange multiple patterns together over multiple cycles. Takes a variable number of arrays with two elements specifying the number of cycles and the pattern to use.

name: as
desc: Sets properties in a batch.

name: asym
desc: Asymmetrical diode distortion

name: attack
desc: Amplitude envelope attack time: Specifies how long it takes for the sound to reach its peak value, relative to the onset.

name: bank
desc: Select the sound bank to use. To be used together with s. The bank name (+ "_") will be prepended to the value of s.
ex: s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").bank('RolandTR909') // = s("RolandTR909_bd RolandTR909_sd")

name: beat
desc: creates a structure pattern from divisions of a cycle especially useful for creating rhythms

name: begin
desc: A pattern of numbers from 0 to 1. Skips the beginning of each sample, e.g. 0.25 to cut off the first quarter from each sample.

params.name: amount
params.desc: between 0 and 1, where 1 is the length of the sample

name: berlin
desc: Generates a continuous pattern of [berlin noise](conceived by Jame Coyne and Jade Rowland as a joke but turned out to be surprisingly cool and useful, like perlin noise but with sawtooth waves), in the range 0..1.

name: binary
desc: Creates a binary pattern from a number.

name: binaryL
desc: Creates a binary list pattern from a number.

params.name: n
params.desc: input number to convert to binary s("saw").seg(8) .partials(binaryL(irand(4096).add(1)))

name: binaryN
desc: Creates a binary pattern from a number, padded to n bits long.

name: binaryNL
desc: Creates a binary list pattern from a number, padded to n bits long.

name: bite
desc: Splits a pattern into the given number of slices, and plays them according to a pattern of slice numbers. Similar to slice, but slices up patterns rather than sound samples.

name: bmod
desc:
Modulates with the output from a given bus. Can be called in sequence like pat.bmod(...).bmod(...) to set up multiple modulators

Send to an audio bus with otherPat.bus(..).

There are two ways to declare which control will be modulated:

  1. Explicitly put control in the config (e.g. bmod({ id: 2, c: "lpf" }))
  2. If the control parameter is absent, the control immediately before the bmod call will be used (e.g. s("saw").lpf(500).bmod({ id: 2 }) to modulate lpf)

Modulators can be referred to by id so that they can be updated later e.g. inside a sometimes. See example below.

params.name: config.subControl
params.desc: Sub-control name to append to the control key. Aliases: sc

name: bpattack
desc: Sets the attack duration for the bandpass filter envelope.

name: bpdc
desc: DC offset of the LFO for the bandpass filter

name: bpdecay
desc: Sets the decay duration for the bandpass filter envelope.

name: bpdepth
desc: Depth of the LFO for the bandpass filter

name: bpdepthfrequency
desc: Depth of the LFO for the bandpass filter, in HZ

name: bpenv
desc: Sets the bandpass filter envelope modulation depth.

params.name: modulation
params.desc: depth of the bandpass filter envelope between 0 and n

name: bpf
desc: Sets the center frequency of the band-pass filter. When using mininotation, you can also optionally supply the 'bpq' parameter separated by ':'.

name: bpq
desc: Sets the band-pass q-factor (resonance).

name: bprate
desc: Rate of the LFO for the bandpass filter

name: bprelease
desc: Sets the release time for the bandpass filter envelope.

name: bpshape
desc: Shape of the LFO for the bandpass filter

name: bpskew
desc: Skew of the LFO for the bandpass filter

params.name: skew
params.desc: How much to bend the LFO shape

name: bpsustain
desc: Sets the sustain amplitude for the bandpass filter envelope.

name: bpsync
desc: Cycle-synced rate of the LFO for the bandpass filter

name: brak
desc: Returns a new pattern where every other cycle is played once, twice as fast, and offset in time by one quarter of a cycle. Creates a kind of breakbeat feel.

name: brand
desc: A continuous pattern of 0 or 1 (binary random)

name: brandBy
desc: A continuous pattern of 0 or 1 (binary random), with a probability for the value being 1

name: bus
desc:
A bus is a send which can be used for mixing patterns. It combines with.. s("bus") to play that bus through another pattern (for, say, applying non-linear effects like distortion to multiple signals)

otherPat.bmod(..) (to modulate another pattern with the bus)

name: busgain
desc: Postgain multiplier prior to sending the signal to the audio bus.

name: byteBeatExpression
desc: Create byte beats with custom expressions

name: byteBeatStartTime
desc: Create byte beats with custom expressions

name: cat
desc: The given items are concatenated, where each one takes one cycle.

name: ccn
desc: MIDI control number: Sends a MIDI control change message.

name: ccv
desc: MIDI control value: Sends a MIDI control change message.

name: ceil
desc: Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values set to their mathematical ceiling. E.g. 3.2 replaced with 4, and -4.2 replaced with -4.

name: channel
desc: Choose the channel the pattern is sent to in superdirt

name: channels
desc: Allows you to set the output channels on the interface

name: chebyshev
desc: Distortion via Chebyshev polynomials

name: choose
desc: Chooses from the given list of values (or patterns of values), according to the pattern that the method is called on. The pattern should be in the range 0 .. 1.

name: choose2
desc: As with choose, but the pattern that this method is called on should be in the range -1 .. 1

name: chooseCycles
desc: Picks one of the elements at random each cycle.

name: chooseInWith
desc: As with {chooseWith}, but the structure comes from the chosen values, rather than the pattern you're using to choose with.

name: chooseWith
desc: Choose from the list of values (or patterns of values) using the given pattern of numbers, which should be in the range of 0..1

name: chop
desc: Cuts each sample into the given number of parts, allowing you to explore a technique known as 'granular synthesis'. It turns a pattern of samples into a pattern of parts of samples.
ex:
samples({ rhodes: 'https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/132/132051_316502-lq.mp3' })
s("rhodes")
 .chop(4)
 .rev() // reverse order of chops
 .loopAt(2) // fit sample into 2 cycles

name: chord
desc: The chord to voice

params.name: symbols
params.desc: chord symbols to voice e.g., C, Eb, Fm7, G7. The symbols can be defined via addVoicings

ex: chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>").voicing()

name: chorus
desc: mix control for the chorus effect

name: chunk
desc: Divides a pattern into a given number of parts, then cycles through those parts in turn, applying the given function to each part in turn (one part per cycle).

name: chunkBack
desc: Like chunk, but cycles through the parts in reverse order. Known as chunk' in tidalcycles

name: chunkBackInto
desc: Like chunkInto, but moves backwards through the chunks.
ex:
sound("bd sd ht lt bd - cp lt").chunkInto(4, hurry(2))
  .bank("tr909")

name: chunkInto
desc: Like chunk, but the function is applied to a looped subcycle of the source pattern.
ex:
sound("bd sd ht lt bd - cp lt").chunkInto(4, hurry(2))
  .bank("tr909")

name: clip
desc: Multiplies the duration with the given number. Also cuts samples off at the end if they exceed the duration.

name: coarse
desc: Fake-resampling for lowering the sample rate. Caution: This effect seems to only work in chromium based browsers

params.name: factor
params.desc: 1 for original 2 for half, 3 for a third and so on.

name: color
desc: Sets the color of the hap in visualizations like pianoroll or highlighting.

name: compress
desc: Compress each cycle into the given timespan, leaving a gap
ex:
cat(
  s("bd sd").compress(.25,.75),
  s("~ bd sd ~")
)

name: compressor
desc: Dynamics Compressor. The params are compressor("threshold:ratio:knee:attack:release") More info here

name: contract
desc:
Experimental

Contracts the step size of the pattern by the given factor. See also expand.

name: control
desc: MIDI control: Sends a MIDI control change message.

name: cosine
desc: A cosine signal between 0 and 1.

name: cosine2
desc: A cosine signal between -1 and 1 (like cosine, but bipolar).

name: cpm
desc: Plays the pattern at the given cycles per minute.

name: crush
desc: Bit crusher effect.

params.name: depth
params.desc: between 1 (for drastic reduction in bit-depth) to 16 (for barely no reduction).

name: cubic
desc: Cubic polynomial distortion

name: cut
desc: In the style of classic drum-machines, cut will stop a playing sample as soon as another samples with in same cutgroup is to be played. An example would be an open hi-hat followed by a closed one, essentially muting the open.

name: cyclesPer
desc: A pattern measuring the duration of events, in cycles per event. cyclesPer doesn't have structure itself, but takes structure, and therefore event durations, from the pattern that it is combined with. For example cyclesPer.struct("1 1 [1 1] 1") would give the same as "0.25 0.25 [0.125 0.125] 0.25". See also its reciprocal, per, also known as perCycle.
ex:
sound("bd sd [bd bd] sd*4 [- sd] [bd [bd bd]]")
  .note(cyclesPer.add(20))

name: decay
desc: Amplitude envelope decay time: the time it takes after the attack time to reach the sustain level. Note that the decay is only audible if the sustain value is lower than 1.

name: defaultmidimap
desc: configures the default midimap, which is used when no "midimap" port is set

name: degrade
desc: Randomly removes 50% of events from the pattern. Shorthand for .degradeBy(0.5)

name: degradeBy
desc: Randomly removes events from the pattern by a given amount. 0 = 0% chance of removal 1 = 100% chance of removal

name: delay
desc:
Sets the level of the delay signal.

When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'delaytime' and 'delayfeedback' parameter, separated by ':'.

name: delayfeedback
desc: Sets the level of the signal that is fed back into the delay. Caution: Values >= 1 will result in a signal that gets louder and louder! Don't do it

name: delayspeed
desc: Sets the time of the delay effect.

params.name: delayspeed
params.desc: controls the pitch of the delay feedback

name: delaysync
desc: Sets the time of the delay effect in cycles.

name: density
desc: Noise crackle density

name: detune
desc: Set detune for stacked voices of supported oscillators
ex: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").detune("<.1 .2 .5 24.1>")

name: dictionary
desc: Which dictionary to use for the voicings. This falls back to the default dictionary if not provided

params.name: dictionaryName
params.desc: which dictionary (having been defined with addVoicings) to use

ex:
addVoicings('house', {
'': ['7 12 16', '0 7 16', '4 7 12'],
'm': ['0 3 7']
})
chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>")
.dict('house').anchor(66)
.voicing().room(.5)

name: diode
desc: Diode-emulating distortion

name: distort
desc: Wave shaping distortion. CAUTION: it can get loud. Second option in optional array syntax (ex: ".9:.5") applies a postgain to the output. Third option sets the waveshaping type. Most useful values are usually between 0 and 10 (depending on source gain). If you are feeling adventurous, you can turn it up to 11 and beyond ;)

name: distorttype
desc: Type of waveshaping distortion to apply.
ex:
s("sine").note("F1*2").release(1)
  .penv(24).pdecay(0.05)
  .distort(rand.range(1, 8))
  .distorttype("<fold chebyshev scurve diode asym sinefold>")

name: distortvol
desc: Postgain for waveshaping distortion.

name: div
desc: Divides each number by the given factor.

name: djf
desc: DJ filter, below 0.5 is low pass filter, above is high pass filter.

params.name: cutoff
params.desc: below 0.5 is low pass filter, above is high pass filter

name: drawLine
desc:
Intended for a debugging, drawLine renders the pattern as a string, where each character represents the same time span. Should only be used with single characters as values, otherwise the character slots will be messed up. Character legend:

  • "|" cycle separator
  • "-" hold previous value
  • "." silence

name: drive
desc: Filter overdrive for supported filter types
ex: note("{f g g c d a a#}%16".sub(17)).s("supersaw").lpenv(8).lpf(150).lpq(.8).ftype('ladder').drive("<.5 4>")

name: drop
desc:
Experimental

Drops the given number of steps from a pattern. A positive number will drop steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

name: dry
desc: Set dryness of reverb. See room and size for more information about reverb.

name: duckattack
desc:
The time required for the ducked signal(s) to return to their normal volume.

Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckonset("0:0.003"). Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. duckorbit("2:3").

name: duckdepth
desc:
The amount of ducking applied to target orbit

Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckdepth("0.3:0.1"). Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. duckorbit("2:3").

name: duckonset
desc:
The time required for the ducked signal(s) to reach their lowest volume. Can be used to prevent clicking or for creative rhythmic effects.

Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckonset("0:0.003"). Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. duckorbit("2:3").
ex:
// Rhythmic
noise: s("pink").distort("2:1").orbit(4) // used rhythmically with 0.3 onset below
hhat: s("hh*16").orbit(7)
ducker: s("bd*4").bank("tr909").duckorbit("4:7").duckonset("0.3:0.003").duckattack(0.25)

name: duckorbit
desc:
Modulate the amplitude of an orbit to create a "sidechain" like effect.

Can be applied to multiple orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckorbit("2:3")

name: duration
desc: Sets the duration of the event in cycles. Similar to clip / legato, it also cuts samples off at the end if they exceed the duration.

name: early
desc: Nudge a pattern to start earlier in time. Equivalent of Tidal's <~ operator

name: echo
desc: Superimpose and offset multiple times, gradually decreasing the velocity

name: echoWith
desc: Superimpose and offset multiple times, applying the given function each time.

params.name: func
params.desc: function to apply, given the pattern and the iteration index

name: end
desc: The same as .begin, but cuts off the end off each sample.

params.name: length
params.desc: 1 = whole sample, .5 = half sample, .25 = quarter sample etc..

name: env
desc:
Configures an envelope. Can be called in sequence like pat.env(...).env(...) to set up multiple envelopes There are two ways to declare which control will be modulated:

  1. Explicitly put control in the config (e.g. env({ c: "lpf" }))
  2. If the control parameter is absent, the control immediately before the env call will be used (e.g. s("saw").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 }) to modulate lpf)

Modulators can be referred to by id so that they can be updated later e.g. inside a sometimes. See example below.

params.name: config.subControl
params.desc: Sub-control name to append to the control key. Aliases: sc

params.name: config.attack
params.desc: Time to reach depth. Aliases: att, a

params.name: config.decay
params.desc: Time to reach sustain. Aliases: dec, d

params.name: config.release
params.desc: Time to return to nominal value. Aliases: rel, r

params.name: config.acurve
params.desc: Snappiness of attack curve (-1 = relaxed, 1 = snappy). Aliases: ac

params.name: config.dcurve
params.desc: Snappiness of decay curve (-1 = relaxed, 1 = snappy). Aliases: dc

params.name: config.rcurve
params.desc: Snappiness of release curve (-1 = relaxed, 1 = snappy). Aliases: rc

ex:
s("pulse").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 })
  .env({ c: "s", a: 1 })
  .diode(0.3)
  .sometimes(x => x.env({ a: "0.5" }, 1)) // envelope #1 (0-indexed)

s("pulse").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 }, 'lpf_mod')
  .env({ c: "s", a: 1 })
  .diode(0.3)
  .sometimes(x => x.env({ a: "0.5" }, 'lpf_mod'))

name: euclid
desc: Changes the structure of the pattern to form an Euclidean rhythm. Euclidean rhythms are rhythms obtained using the greatest common divisor of two numbers. They were described in 2004 by Godfried Toussaint, a Canadian computer scientist. Euclidean rhythms are really useful for computer/algorithmic music because they can describe a large number of rhythms with a couple of numbers.

name: euclidish
desc: A 'euclid' variant with an additional parameter that morphs the resulting rhythm from 0 (no morphing) to 1 (completely 'even'). For example sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0) would be the same as sound("bd").euclid(3,8), and sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,1) would be the same as sound("bd bd bd"). sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0.5) would have a groove somewhere between. Inspired by the work of Malcom Braff.

params.name: groove
params.desc: exists between the extremes of 0 (straight euclidian) and 1 (straight pulse)

name: euclidLegato
desc: Similar to euclid, but each pulse is held until the next pulse, so there will be no gaps.

name: euclidLegatoRot
desc: Similar to euclid, but each pulse is held until the next pulse, so there will be no gaps, and has an additional parameter for 'rotating' the resulting sequence

name: euclidRot
desc: Like euclid, but has an additional parameter for 'rotating' the resulting sequence.
ex:
// A Samba rhythm necklace from Brazil
note("c3").euclidRot(3,16,14)

name: every
desc: An alias for firstOf

name: expand
desc:
Experimental

Expands the step size of the pattern by the given factor.

name: extend
desc:
Experimental

extend is similar to fast in that it increases its density, but it also increases the step count accordingly. So stepcat("a b".extend(2), "c d") would be the same as "a b a b c d", whereas stepcat("a b".fast(2), "c d") would be the same as "[a b] [a b] c d".
ex:
stepcat(
  sound("bd bd - cp").extend(2),
  sound("bd - sd -")
).pace(8)

name: fanchor
desc: controls the center of the filter envelope. 0 is unipolar positive, .5 is bipolar, 1 is unipolar negative
ex:
note("{f g g c d a a#}%8").s("sawtooth").lpf("{1000}%2")
.lpenv(8).fanchor("<0 .5 1>")

name: fast
desc: Speed up a pattern by the given factor. Used by "*" in mini notation.
ex: s("bd hh sd hh").fast(2) // s("[bd hh sd hh]*2")

name: fastChunk
desc: Like chunk, but the cycles of the source pattern aren't repeated for each set of chunks.

name: fastGap
desc: speeds up a pattern like fast, but rather than it playing multiple times as fast would it instead leaves a gap in the remaining space of the cycle. For example, the following will play the sound pattern "bd sn" only once but compressed into the first half of the cycle, i.e. twice as fast.

name: filter
desc: Filters haps using the given function

name: filterWhen
desc: Filters haps by their begin time

name: firstOf
desc: Applies the given function every n cycles, starting from the first cycle.

name: fit
desc: Makes the sample fit its event duration. Good for rhythmical loops like drum breaks. Similar to loopAt.

name: floor
desc: Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values set to their mathematical floor. E.g. 3.7 replaced with to 3, and -4.2 replaced with -5.

name: fmattack
desc:
Attack time for the FM envelope: time it takes to reach maximum modulation

A number may be added afterwards to control the attack of the envelope of any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmatt5)
ex:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmattack("<0 .05 .1 .2>")
._scope()

name: fmdecay
desc:
Decay time for the FM envelope: seconds until the sustain level is reached after the attack phase.

A number may be added afterwards to control the decay of the envelope of any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmdec6)
ex:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay("<.01 .05 .1 .2>")
.fmsustain(.4)
._scope()

name: fmenv
desc:
Ramp type of fm envelope. Exp might be a bit broken..

A number may be added afterwards to control the envelope of any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmenv4)
ex:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay(.2)
.fmsustain(0)
.fmenv("<exp lin>")
._scope()

name: fmh
desc:
Sets the Frequency Modulation Harmonicity Ratio. Controls the timbre of the sound. Whole numbers and simple ratios sound more natural, while decimal numbers and complex ratios sound metallic.

A number may be added afterwards to control the harmonicity of any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmh2)
ex:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmh("<1 2 1.5 1.61>")
._scope()

name: fmi
desc:
Sets the Frequency Modulation of the synth. Controls the modulation index, which defines the brightness of the sound.

A number may be added afterwards to control the modulation index of any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fm3). Also, FMs may be routed into each other with matrix commands like fm13, which would send fm1 back into fm3
ex:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm("<0 1 2 8 32>")
._scope()

name: fmrelease
desc:
Release time for the FM envelope: how much modulation is applied after the note is released

A number may be added afterwards to control the release of the envelope of any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmrel8)

name: fmsustain
desc:
Sustain level for the FM envelope: how much modulation is applied after the decay phase

A number may be added afterwards to control the sustain of the envelope of any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmsus7)
ex:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay(.1)
.fmsustain("<1 .75 .5 0>")
._scope()

name: fmwave
desc:
Waveform of the fm modulator

A number may be added afterwards to control the waveform any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmwave6)

name: focus
desc: Similar to compress, but doesn't leave gaps, and the 'focus' can be bigger than a cycle

name: fold
desc: Wavefolding distortion

name: freq
desc: Set frequency of sound.

params.name: frequency
params.desc: in Hz. the audible range is between 20 and 20000 Hz

name: fromBipolar
desc: Assumes a numerical pattern, containing bipolar values in the range -1 .. 1 Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the unipolar range 0 .. 1

name: fscope
desc: Renders an oscilloscope for the frequency domain of the audio signal.

params.name: color
params.desc: line color as hex or color name. defaults to white.

params.name: pos
params.desc: y-position relative to screen height. 0 = top, 1 = bottom of screen

name: ftype
desc: Sets the filter type. The ladder filter is more aggressive. More types might be added in the future.
ex: note("{f g g c d a a#}%8").s("sawtooth").lpenv(4).lpf(500).ftype("<0 1 2>").lpq(1)

note("c f g g a c d4").fast(2)
.sound('sawtooth')
.lpf(200).fanchor(0)
.lpenv(3).lpq(1)
.ftype("<ladder 12db 24db>")

name: gain
desc: Controls the gain by an exponential amount.

name: gravityX
desc: The device's gravity x-axis value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: gravityY
desc: The device's gravity y-axis value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: gravityZ
desc: The device's gravity z-axis value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: grow
desc:
Experimental

Progressively grows the pattern by 'n' steps until the full pattern is played, or if a second value is given (using mininotation list syntax with :), that number of times. A positive number will progressively grow steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

name: hard
desc: Hard-clipping distortion

name: hpattack
desc: Sets the attack duration for the highpass filter envelope.

name: hpdc
desc: DC offset of the LFO for the highpass filter

name: hpdecay
desc: Sets the decay duration for the highpass filter envelope.

name: hpdepth
desc: Depth of the LFO for the highpass filter

name: hpdepthfrequency
desc: Depth of the LFO for the hipass filter, in hz

name: hpenv
desc: Sets the highpass filter envelope modulation depth.

params.name: modulation
params.desc: depth of the highpass filter envelope between 0 and n

name: hpf
desc:
Applies the cutoff frequency of the high-pass filter.

When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'hpq' parameter, separated by ':'.

name: hpq
desc: Controls the high-pass q-value.

name: hprate
desc: Rate of the LFO for the highpass filter

name: hprelease
desc: Sets the release time for the highpass filter envelope.

name: hpshape
desc: Shape of the LFO for the highpass filter

name: hpskew
desc: Skew of the LFO for the highpass filter

params.name: skew
params.desc: How much to bend the LFO shape

name: hpsustain
desc: Sets the sustain amplitude for the highpass filter envelope.

name: hpsync
desc: Cycle-synced rate of the LFO for the highpass filter

name: hurry
desc: Both speeds up the pattern (like 'fast') and the sample playback (like 'speed').

name: hush
desc: Silences a pattern.

name: inhabit
desc: Picks patterns (or plain values) either from a list (by index) or a lookup table (by name). Similar to pick, but cycles are squeezed into the target ('inhabited') pattern.

name: inhabitmod
desc: The same as inhabit, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value. For example, if you pick the fifth pattern of a list of three, you'll get the second one.

name: inside
desc: Carries out an operation 'inside' a cycle.

name: invert
desc: Swaps 1s and 0s in a binary pattern.

name: irand
desc: A continuous pattern of random integers, between 0 and n-1.
ex:
// randomly select scale notes from 0 - 7 (= C to C)
n(irand(8)).struct("x x*2 x x*3").scale("C:minor")

name: irbegin
desc: Sets the beginning of the IR response sample

name: iresponse
desc: Sets the sample to use as an impulse response for the reverb.

name: irspeed
desc: Sets speed of the sample for the impulse response.

name: isaw
desc: A sawtooth signal between 1 and 0 (like saw, but flipped).

name: isaw2
desc: A sawtooth signal between 1 and -1 (like saw2, but flipped).

name: iter
desc: Divides a pattern into a given number of subdivisions, plays the subdivisions in order, but increments the starting subdivision each cycle. The pattern wraps to the first subdivision after the last subdivision is played.

name: iterBack
desc: Like iter, but plays the subdivisions in reverse order. Known as iter' in tidalcycles

name: itri
desc: An inverted triangle signal between 1 and 0 (like tri, but flipped).

name: itri2
desc: An inverted triangle signal between -1 and 1 (like itri, but bipolar).

name: jux
desc: The jux function creates strange stereo effects, by applying a function to a pattern, but only in the right-hand channel.
ex: s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(rev)
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(press)
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(iter(4))

name: juxBy
desc: Jux with adjustable stereo width. 0 = mono, 1 = full stereo.
ex: s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").juxBy("<0 .5 1>/2", rev)

name: keyDown
desc: returns true when a key or array of keys is held Key name reference

name: label
desc: Sets the displayed text for an event on the pianoroll

name: lastOf
desc: Applies the given function every n cycles, starting from the last cycle.

name: late
desc: Nudge a pattern to start later in time. Equivalent of Tidal's ~> operator

name: layer
desc: Layers the result of the given function(s). Like superimpose, but without the original pattern:

name: leslie
desc: Emulation of a Leslie speaker: speakers rotating in a wooden amplified cabinet.

name: lfo
desc:
Configures an LFO. Can be called in sequence like pat.lfo(...).lfo(...) to set up multiple LFOs. There are two ways to declare which control will be modulated:

  1. Explicitly put control in the config (e.g. lfo({ c: "lpf" }))
  2. If the control parameter is absent, the control immediately before the lfo call will be used (e.g. s("saw").lpf(500).lfo() to modulate lpf)

Modulators can be referred to by id so that they can be updated later e.g. inside a sometimes. See example below.

params.name: config.subControl
params.desc: Sub-control name to append to the control key. Aliases: sc

params.name: config.dcoffset
params.desc: DC offset / bias for the waveform. Aliases: dc

name: linger
desc: Selects the given fraction of the pattern and repeats that part to fill the remainder of the cycle.

name: lock
desc: Specifies whether delaytime is calculated relative to cps.

params.name: enable
params.desc: When set to 1, delaytime is a direct multiple of a cycle.

name: log
desc: Writes the content of the current event to the console (visible in the side menu).

name: logValues
desc: A simplified version of log which writes all "values" (various configurable parameters) within the event to the console (visible in the side menu).

name: loop
desc: Loops the sample. Note that the tempo of the loop is not synced with the cycle tempo. To change the loop region, use loopBegin / loopEnd.

name: loopAt
desc: Makes the sample fit the given number of cycles by changing the speed.

name: loopAtCps
desc: Makes the sample fit the given number of cycles and cps value, by changing the speed. Please note that at some point cps will be given by a global clock and this function will be deprecated/removed.

name: loopBegin
desc: Begin to loop at a specific point in the sample (inbetween begin and end). Note that the loop point must be inbetween begin and end, and before loopEnd! Note: Samples starting with wt_ will automatically loop! (wt = wavetable)

params.name: time
params.desc: between 0 and 1, where 1 is the length of the sample

name: loopEnd
desc: End the looping section at a specific point in the sample (inbetween begin and end). Note that the loop point must be inbetween begin and end, and after loopBegin!

params.name: time
params.desc: between 0 and 1, where 1 is the length of the sample

name: lpattack
desc: Sets the attack duration for the lowpass filter envelope.

name: lpdc
desc: DC offset of the LFO for the lowpass filter

name: lpdecay
desc: Sets the decay duration for the lowpass filter envelope.

name: lpdepth
desc: Depth of the LFO for the lowpass filter

name: lpdepthfrequency
desc: Depth of the LFO for the lowpass filter, in HZ

name: lpenv
desc: Sets the lowpass filter envelope modulation depth.

params.name: modulation
params.desc: depth of the lowpass filter envelope between 0 and n

name: lpf
desc:
Applies the cutoff frequency of the low-pass filter.

When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'lpq' parameter, separated by ':'.

name: lpq
desc: Controls the low-pass q-value.

name: lprate
desc: Rate of the LFO for the lowpass filter

name: lprelease
desc: Sets the release time for the lowpass filter envelope.

name: lpshape
desc: Shape of the LFO for the lowpass filter

name: lpskew
desc: Skew of the LFO for the lowpass filter

params.name: skew
params.desc: How much to bend the LFO shape

name: lpsustain
desc: Sets the sustain amplitude for the lowpass filter envelope.

name: lpsync
desc: Cycle-synced rate of the LFO for the lowpass filter

name: lrate
desc: Rate of modulation / rotation for leslie effect

name: lsize
desc: Physical size of the cabinet in meters. Be careful, it might be slightly larger than your computer. Affects the Doppler amount (pitch warble)

name: mask
desc: Returns silence when mask is 0 or "~"

name: midi
desc: MIDI output: Opens a MIDI output port.

params.name: midiport
params.desc: MIDI device name or index defaulting to 0

ex: note("c4").midichan(1).midi('IAC Driver Bus 1', { controller: true, latency: 50 })

name: midibend
desc: MIDI pitch bend: Sends a MIDI pitch bend message.

name: midichan
desc: MIDI channel: Sets the MIDI channel for the event.

name: midicmd
desc: MIDI command: Sends a MIDI command message.

name: midikeys
desc:
MIDI keyboard: Opens a MIDI input port to receive MIDI keyboard messages.

The note length is fixed as Superdough is not currently set up for undetermined note durations

params.name: input
params.desc: MIDI device name or index defaulting to 0

ex:
const kb = await midikeys('Arturia KeyStep 32')
kb("0.5 1")
  .s("saw")
  .add(note(rand.mul(0.3)))
  .lpf(1000).lpe(2).room(0.5)

name: midimaps
desc: Adds midimaps to the registry. Inside each midimap, control names (e.g. lpf) are mapped to cc numbers.
ex:
midimaps({ mymap: { lpf: 74 } })
$: note("c a f e")
.lpf(sine.slow(4))
.midimap('mymap')
.midi()

name: midin
desc:
MIDI input: Opens a MIDI input port to receive MIDI control change messages.

The output is a function that accepts a midi cc value to query as well as (optionally) a midi channel

params.name: input
params.desc: MIDI device name or index defaulting to 0

ex:
const cc = await midin('IAC Driver Bus 1')
note("c a f e").lpf(cc(0).range(0, 1000)).lpq(cc(1).range(0, 10)).sound("sawtooth")

const allCC = await midin('IAC Driver Bus 1')
const cc = (ccNum) => allCC(ccNum, 2) // just channel 2
note("c a f e").s("saw")
  .when(cc(0).gt(0), x => x.postgain(0))

name: midiport
desc: MIDI port: Sets the MIDI port for the event.

name: miditouch
desc: MIDI key after touch: Sends a MIDI key after touch message.

name: mode
desc: Remove anchor note from the voicing. Useful for melody harmonization

name: morph
desc: Takes two binary rhythms represented as lists of 1s and 0s, and a number between 0 and 1 that morphs between them. The two lists should contain the same number of true values.

name: mousex
desc: The mouse's x position value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: mousey
desc: The mouse's y position value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: mul
desc: Multiplies each number by the given factor.

name: n
desc: Selects the given index from the sample map. Numbers too high will wrap around. n can also be used to play midi numbers, but it is recommended to use note instead.

name: never
desc: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0, fn) (never calls fn)

name: noise
desc: Adds pink noise to the mix

name: note
desc:
Plays the given note name or midi number. A note name consists of

  • a letter (a-g or A-G)
  • optional accidentals (b or #)
  • optional (possibly negative) octave number (0-9). Defaults to 3

Examples of valid note names: c, bb, Bb, f#, c3, A4, Eb2, c#5

You can also use midi numbers instead of note names, where 69 is mapped to A4 440Hz in 12EDO.

name: nrpnn
desc: MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter number: Sends a MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter number message.

name: nrpv
desc: MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter value: Sends a MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter value message.

name: octave
desc: Sets the default octave of a synth.

name: octaves
desc: How many octaves are voicing steps spread apart, defaults to 1
ex: chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>").octaves("<2 4>").voicing()

name: off
desc: Superimposes the function result on top of the original pattern, delayed by the given time.

name: offset
desc: Sets how the voicing is offset from the anchored position

params.name: shift
params.desc: the amount to shift the voicing up or down

ex: chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>").offset("<0 1 2 3 4 5>") // alter the voicing each time

name: often
desc: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0.75, fn)

name: orbit
desc: An orbit is a global parameter context for patterns. Patterns with the same orbit will share the same global effects.

name: orientationAlpha
desc: The device's orientation alpha value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: orientationBeta
desc: The device's orientation beta value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: orientationGamma
desc: The device's orientation gamma value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: osc
desc: Sends each hap as an OSC message, which can be picked up by SuperCollider or any other OSC-enabled software. For more info, read MIDI & OSC in the docs

name: oschost
desc: The host to send open sound control messages to. Requires running the OSC bridge.

name: oscport
desc: The port to send open sound control messages to. Requires running the OSC bridge.

name: outside
desc: Carries out an operation 'outside' a cycle.

name: pace
desc:
Experimental

Speeds a pattern up or down, to fit to the given number of steps per cycle.
ex:
sound("bd sd cp").pace(4)
// The same as sound("{bd sd cp}%4") or sound("<bd sd cp>*4")

name: palindrome
desc: Applies rev to a pattern every other cycle, so that the pattern alternates between forwards and backwards.

name: pan
desc: Sets position in stereo.

params.name: pan
params.desc: between 0 and 1, from left to right (assuming stereo), once round a circle (assuming multichannel)

ex: s("bd rim sd rim bd ~ cp rim").pan(sine.slow(2))

name: panchor
desc:
Sets the range anchor of the envelope:

  • anchor 0: range = [note, note + penv]
  • anchor 1: range = [note - penv, note] If you don't set an anchor, the value will default to the psustain value.

name: partials
desc:
Scale the magnitude of the harmonics of one of the core synths ('sine', 'tri', 'saw', ..)

Can also be used to create a new synth via s('user').partials(...)

params.name: magnitudes
params.desc: List of [0, 1] magnitudes for partials. 0th entry is the fundamental harmonic (i.e. DC offset is skipped)

name: pattack
desc: Attack time of pitch envelope.

name: pcurve
desc: Curve of envelope. Defaults to linear. exponential is good for kicks

name: pdecay
desc: Decay time of pitch envelope.

name: penv
desc: Amount of pitch envelope. Negative values will flip the envelope. If you don't set other pitch envelope controls, pattack:.2 will be the default.

name: per
desc: A pattern measuring the 'shortness' of events, or in other words, the duration of pattern events, in events per cycle. per doesn't have structure itself, but takes structure, and therefore event durations, from the pattern that it is combined with. For example per.struct("1 1 [1 1] 1") would give the same as "4 4 [8 8] 4". See also its reciprocal, cyclesPer.

name: perlin
desc: Generates a continuous pattern of perlin noise, in the range 0..1.

name: perx
desc: Like per but measures the shortness of events according to an exponential curve. In particular, where the event duration halves, the returned value increases by one. perx.struct("1 1 [1 [1 1]] 1") would therefore be the same as "3 3 [4 [5 5]] 3".

name: phaser
desc: Phaser audio effect that approximates popular guitar pedals.

name: phasercenter
desc: The center frequency of the phaser in HZ. Defaults to 1000

name: phaserdepth
desc: The amount the signal is affected by the phaser effect. Defaults to 0.75

name: phasersweep
desc: The frequency sweep range of the lfo for the phaser effect. Defaults to 2000

name: phases
desc: Rotates the harmonics of one of the core synths ('sine', 'tri', 'saw', 'user', ..) by a list of phases

params.name: phases
params.desc: List of [0, 1) phases for partials. 0th entry is the fundamental phase (i.e. DC offset is skipped)

name: pianoroll
desc: Visualises a pattern as a scrolling 'pianoroll', displayed in the background of the editor. To show a pianoroll for all running patterns, use all(pianoroll). To have a pianoroll appear below a pattern instead, prefix with _, e.g.: sound("bd sd")._pianoroll().

params.name: options
params.desc: Object containing all the optional following parameters as key value pairs:

params.name: cycles
params.desc: number of cycles to be displayed at the same time - defaults to 4

params.name: playhead
params.desc: location of the active notes on the time axis - 0 to 1, defaults to 0.5

params.name: labels
params.desc: displays labels on individual notes (see the label function) - 0 by default

params.name: flipTime
params.desc: reverse the direction of the roll - 0 by default

params.name: flipValues
params.desc: reverse the relative location of notes on the value axis - 0 by default

params.name: overscan
params.desc: lookup X cycles outside of the cycles window to display notes in advance - 1 by default

params.name: hideNegative
params.desc: hide notes with negative time (before starting playing the pattern) - 0 by default

params.name: smear
params.desc: notes leave a solid trace - 0 by default

params.name: fold
params.desc: notes takes the full value axis width - 0 by default

params.name: active
params.desc: hexadecimal or CSS color of the active notes - defaults to #FFCA28

params.name: inactive
params.desc: hexadecimal or CSS color of the inactive notes - defaults to #7491D2

params.name: background
params.desc: hexadecimal or CSS color of the background - defaults to transparent

params.name: playheadColor
params.desc: hexadecimal or CSS color of the line representing the play head - defaults to white

params.name: fill
params.desc: notes are filled with color (otherwise only the label is displayed) - 0 by default

params.name: fillActive
params.desc: active notes are filled with color - 0 by default

params.name: stroke
params.desc: notes are shown with colored borders - 0 by default

params.name: strokeActive
params.desc: active notes are shown with colored borders - 0 by default

params.name: hideInactive
params.desc: only active notes are shown - 0 by default

params.name: colorizeInactive
params.desc: use note color for inactive notes - 1 by default

params.name: fontFamily
params.desc: define the font used by notes labels - defaults to 'monospace'

params.name: minMidi
params.desc: minimum note value to display on the value axis - defaults to 10

params.name: maxMidi
params.desc: maximum note value to display on the value axis - defaults to 90

params.name: autorange
params.desc: automatically calculate the minMidi and maxMidi parameters - 0 by default

name: pick
desc: Picks patterns (or plain values) either from a list (by index) or a lookup table (by name). Similar to inhabit, but maintains the structure of the original patterns.
ex: note("<0 1 2!2 3>".pick(["g a", "e f", "f g f g" , "g c d"]))

name: pickF
desc: pickF lets you use a pattern of numbers to pick which function to apply to another pattern.

params.name: funcs
params.desc: the array of functions from which to pull

name: pickmod
desc: The same as pick, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value. For example, if you pick the fifth pattern of a list of three, you'll get the second one.

name: pickmodF
desc: The same as pickF, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the functions list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

params.name: funcs
params.desc: the array of functions from which to pull

name: pickmodOut
desc: The same as pickOut, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

name: pickmodReset
desc: The same as pickReset, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

name: pickmodRestart
desc: The same as pickRestart, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

name: pickOut
desc: Similar to pick, but it applies an outerJoin instead of an innerJoin.

name: pickReset
desc: Similar to pick, but the choosen pattern is reset when its index is triggered.

name: pickRestart
desc: Similar to pick, but the choosen pattern is restarted when its index is triggered.

name: pitchwheel
desc: Renders a pitch circle to visualize frequencies within one octave

name: ply
desc: The ply function repeats each event the given number of times.

name: plyForEach
desc: The plyForEach function repeats each event the given number of times, applying the given function to each event. This version of ply uses the iteration index as an argument to the function, similar to echoWith.

params.name: func
params.desc: function to apply, given the pattern and the iteration index

name: plyWith
desc: The plyWith function repeats each event the given number of times, applying the given function to each event.\n

name: polymeter
desc:
Experimental

Aligns the steps of the patterns, creating polymeters. The patterns are repeated until they all fit the cycle. For example, in the below the first pattern is repeated twice, and the second is repeated three times, to fit the lowest common multiple of six steps.
ex:
// The same as note("{c eb g, c2 g2}%6")
polymeter("c eb g", "c2 g2").note()

name: postgain
desc: Gain applied after all effects have been processed.

name: prelease
desc: Release time of pitch envelope
ex:
note("<c eb g bb> ~")
.release(.5) // to hear the pitch release
.prelease("<0 .1 .25 .5>")

name: press
desc: Syncopates a rhythm, by shifting each event halfway into its timespan.

name: pressBy
desc: Like press, but allows you to specify the amount by which each event is shifted. pressBy(0.5) is the same as press, while pressBy(1/3) shifts each event by a third of its timespan.

name: progNum
desc: MIDI program number: Sends a MIDI program change message.

name: pure
desc: A discrete value that repeats once per cycle.

name: pw
desc: Controls the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

name: pwrate
desc: Controls the lfo rate for the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

name: pwsweep
desc: Controls the lfo sweep for the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

name: rand
desc: A continuous pattern of random numbers, between 0 and 1.

name: rand2
desc: A continuous pattern of random numbers, between -1 and 1

name: randL
desc: Creates a list of random numbers of the given length

name: range
desc: Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 .. 1. Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range. Most useful in combination with continuous patterns.

name: range2
desc: Assumes a numerical pattern, containing bipolar values in the range -1 .. 1 Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range.

name: rangex
desc: Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 .. 1 Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range, following an exponential curve.

name: rarely
desc: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0.25, fn)

name: ratio
desc: Allows dividing numbers via list notation using ":". Returns a new pattern with just numbers.

name: ref
desc: exposes a custom value at query time. basically allows mutating state without evaluation

name: register
desc: Registers a new pattern method. The method is added to the Pattern class + the standalone function is returned from register.

params.name: name
params.desc: name of the function, or an array of names to be used as synonyms

params.name: func
params.desc: function with 1 or more params, where last is the current pattern

params.name: patternify
params.desc: defaults to true; if set to false, you will have more control over the arguments to func as they will be in their raw form and it will be up to you to patternify them and/or query them for values

name: release
desc: Amplitude envelope release time: The time it takes after the offset to go from sustain level to zero.

name: repeatCycles
desc: Repeats each cycle the given number of times.

name: replicate
desc:
Experimental

replicate is similar to fast in that it increases its density, but it also increases the step count accordingly. So stepcat("a b".replicate(2), "c d") would be the same as "a b a b c d", whereas stepcat("a b".fast(2), "c d") would be the same as "[a b] [a b] c d".

TODO: find out how this function differs from extend
ex:
stepcat(
  sound("bd bd - cp").replicate(2),
  sound("bd - sd -")
).pace(8)

name: rev
desc: Reverse all cycles in a pattern. See also revv for reversing a whole pattern.

name: revv
desc: Reverse a whole pattern. See also rev for reversing each cycle.

name: ribbon
desc: Loops the pattern inside an offset for cycles. If you think of the entire span of time in cycles as a ribbon, you can cut a single piece and loop it.

name: room
desc:
Sets the level of reverb.

When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'size' parameter, separated by ':'.

name: roomdim
desc: Reverb lowpass frequency at -60dB (in hertz). When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

name: roomfade
desc: Reverb fade time (in seconds). When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

name: roomlp
desc: Reverb lowpass starting frequency (in hertz). When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

name: roomsize
desc: Sets the room size of the reverb, see room. When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

name: rootNotes
desc: Maps the chords of the incoming pattern to root notes in the given octave.

name: rotationAlpha
desc: The device's rotation around the alpha-axis value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: rotationBeta
desc: The device's rotation around the beta-axis value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: rotationGamma
desc: The device's rotation around the gamma-axis value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: round
desc: Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values rounded to the nearest integer.

name: run
desc: A discrete pattern of numbers from 0 to n-1

name: s
desc: Select a sound / sample by name. When using mininotation, you can also optionally supply 'n' and 'gain' parameters separated by ':'.

params.name: sound
params.desc: The sound / pattern of sounds to pick

name: samples
desc: Loads a collection of samples to use with s

name: saw
desc: A sawtooth signal between 0 and 1.

name: saw2
desc: A sawtooth signal between -1 and 1 (like saw, but bipolar).

name: scale
desc:
Turns numbers into notes in the scale (zero indexed) or quantizes notes to a scale.

When describing notes via numbers, note that negative numbers can be used to wrap backwards in the scale as well as sharps or flats to produce notes outside of the scale.

Also sets scale for other scale operations, like {@link Pattern#scaleTranspose}.

A scale consists of a root note (e.g. c4, c, f#, bb4) followed by semicolon (':') and then a scale type.

The scale name must be written without spaces (because it would be interpreted as a multi-step pattern otherwise). If your scale name includes spaces, replace them with colons.

The root note defaults to octave 3, if no octave number is given.

name: scaleTranspose
desc: Transposes notes inside the scale by the number of steps. Expected to be called on a Pattern which already has a {@link Pattern#scale}

name: scope
desc: Renders an oscilloscope for the time domain of the audio signal.

params.name: align
params.desc: if 1, the scope will be aligned to the first zero crossing. defaults to 1

params.name: color
params.desc: line color as hex or color name. defaults to white.

params.name: pos
params.desc: y-position relative to screen height. 0 = top, 1 = bottom of screen

params.name: trigger
params.desc: amplitude value that is used to align the scope. defaults to 0.

name: scramble
desc: Slices a pattern into the given number of parts, then plays those parts at random. Similar to shuffle, but parts might be played more than once, or not at all, per cycle.

name: scrub
desc: Allows you to scrub an audio file like a tape loop by passing values that represents the position in the audio file in the optional array syntax ex: "0.5:2", the second value controls the speed of playback

name: seed
desc: Change the seed for random signals. Normally, random signals depend on time, so two patterns at the same time will have the same random values. Specifying a new seed changes the signal output by rand. This also affects other functions that use randomness, like shuffle and sometimes.

params.name: n
params.desc: A new seed. Can be any number.

ex:
$: s("hh*4").degrade();
$: s("bd*4").degrade().seed(1); // Will degrade different events from the hi-hat

name: segment
desc: Samples the pattern at a rate of n events per cycle. Useful for turning a continuous pattern into a discrete one.

name: seq
desc: Like cat, but the items are crammed into one cycle.

name: sequence
desc: See fastcat

name: setcpm
desc: Changes the global tempo to the given cycles per minute

name: setGainCurve
desc: Apply a function to all gains provided in patterns. Can be used to rescale gain to be quadratic, exponential, etc. rather than linear
ex:
setGainCurve((x) => x * x) // quadratic gain
s("bd*4").gain(0.5) // equivalent to 0.25 gain normally

name: setMaxPolyphony
desc: Set the max polyphony. If notes are ringing out via release then they will start to die out in first-in-first-out order once the max polyphony has been hit

name: shape
desc: (Deprecated) Wave shaping distortion. WARNING: can suddenly get unpredictably loud. Please use distort instead, which has a more predictable response curve second option in optional array syntax (ex: ".9:.5") applies a postgain to the output

name: shrink
desc:
Experimental

Progressively shrinks the pattern by 'n' steps until there's nothing left, or if a second value is given (using mininotation list syntax with :), that number of times. A positive number will progressively drop steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

name: shuffle
desc: Slices a pattern into the given number of parts, then plays those parts in random order. Each part will be played exactly once per cycle.

name: silence
desc: Does absolutely nothing..

name: sine
desc: A sine signal between 0 and 1.

name: sine2
desc: A sine signal between -1 and 1 (like sine, but bipolar).

name: sinefold
desc: Wavefolding distortion composed with sinusoid

name: slice
desc: Chops samples into the given number of slices, triggering those slices with a given pattern of slice numbers. Instead of a number, it also accepts a list of numbers from 0 to 1 to slice at specific points.

name: slider
desc: Displays a slider widget to allow the user manipulate a value

name: slow
desc: Slow down a pattern over the given number of cycles. Like the "/" operator in mini notation.
ex: s("bd hh sd hh").slow(2) // s("[bd hh sd hh]/2")

name: slowcat
desc: Concatenation: combines a list of patterns, switching between them successively, one per cycle.

name: soft
desc: Soft-clipping distortion

name: someCycles
desc: Shorthand for .someCyclesBy(0.5, fn)

name: someCyclesBy
desc: Randomly applies the given function by the given probability on a cycle by cycle basis. Similar to sometimesBy

name: sometimes
desc: Applies the given function with a 50% chance

name: sometimesBy
desc: Randomly applies the given function by the given probability. Similar to someCyclesBy

name: soundAlias
desc: Register an alias for a sound.

params.name: alias
params.desc: The alias to use for the sound

name: source
desc: Define a custom webaudio node to use as a sound source.

name: spectrum
desc: Renders a spectrum analyzer for the incoming audio signal.

name: speed
desc: Changes the speed of sample playback, i.e. a cheap way of changing pitch.

params.name: speed
params.desc: inf to inf, negative numbers play the sample backwards.

name: spiral
desc: Displays a spiral visual.

params.name: options
params.desc: Object containing all the optional following parameters as key value pairs:

params.name: stretch
params.desc: controls the rotations per cycle ratio, where 1 = 1 cycle / 360 degrees

params.name: cap
params.desc: style of line ends: butt (default), round, square

params.name: playheadLength
params.desc: length of playhead in rotations, defaults to 0.02

params.name: steady
params.desc: steadyness of spiral vs playhead. 1 = spiral doesn't move, playhead does.

params.name: activeColor
params.desc: color of active segment. defaults to foreground of theme

params.name: inactiveColor
params.desc: color of inactive segments. defaults to gutterForeground of theme

params.name: colorizeInactive
params.desc: wether or not to colorize inactive segments, defaults to 0

params.name: fade
params.desc: wether or not past and future should fade out. defaults to 1

params.name: logSpiral
params.desc: wether or not the spiral should be logarithmic. defaults to 0

name: splice
desc: Works the same as slice, but changes the playback speed of each slice to match the duration of its step.

name: spread
desc: Set the stereo pan spread for supported oscillators
ex: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").spread("<0 .3 1>")

name: square
desc: A square signal between 0 and 1.

name: square2
desc: A square signal between -1 and 1 (like square, but bipolar).

name: squeeze
desc: Pick from the list of values (or patterns of values) via the index using the given pattern of integers. The selected pattern will be compressed to fit the duration of the selecting event
ex: note(squeeze("<0@2 [1!2] 2>", ["g a", "f g f g" , "g a c d"]))

name: squiz
desc:
Made by Calum Gunn. Reminiscent of some weird mixture of filter, ring-modulator and pitch-shifter. The SuperCollider manual defines Squiz as:

"A simplistic pitch-raising algorithm. It's not meant to sound natural; its sound is reminiscent of some weird mixture of filter, ring-modulator and pitch-shifter, depending on the input. The algorithm works by cutting the signal into fragments (delimited by upwards-going zero-crossings) and squeezing those fragments in the time domain (i.e. simply playing them back faster than they came in), leaving silences inbetween. All the parameters apart from memlen can be modulated."

params.name: squiz
params.desc: Try passing multiples of 2 to it - 2, 4, 8 etc.

name: stack
desc: The given items are played at the same time at the same length.

name: stepalt
desc:
Experimental

Concatenates patterns stepwise, according to an inferred 'steps per cycle'. Similar to stepcat, but if an argument is a list, the whole pattern will alternate between the elements in the list.
ex:
stepalt(["bd cp", "mt"], "bd").sound()
// The same as "bd cp bd mt bd".sound()

name: stepcat
desc: 'Concatenates' patterns like fastcat, but proportional to a number of steps per cycle. The steps can either be inferred from the pattern, or provided as a [length, pattern] pair. Has the alias timecat.
ex:
stepcat("bd sd cp","hh hh").sound()
// the same as "bd sd cp hh hh".sound()

name: stretch
desc: Changes the speed of sample playback, i.e. a cheap way of changing pitch.

params.name: factor
params.desc: inf to inf, negative numbers play the sample backwards.

name: striate
desc: Cuts each sample into the given number of parts, triggering progressive portions of each sample at each loop.

name: struct
desc: Applies the given structure to the pattern:
ex:
note("c,eb,g")
  .struct("x ~ x ~ ~ x ~ x ~ ~ ~ x ~ x ~ ~")
  .slow(2)

name: stut
desc: Deprecated. Like echo, but the last 2 parameters are flipped.

name: sub
desc: Like add, but the given numbers are subtracted.
ex:
n("0 2 4".sub("<0 1 2 3>")).scale("C4:minor")
// See add for more information.

name: superimpose
desc: Superimposes the result of the given function(s) on top of the original pattern:

name: sustain
desc: Amplitude envelope sustain level: The level which is reached after attack / decay, being sustained until the offset.

name: swing
desc: Shorthand for swingBy with 1/3:

name: swingBy
desc: The function swingBy x n breaks each cycle into n slices, and then delays events in the second half of each slice by the amount x, which is relative to the size of the (half) slice. So if x is 0 it does nothing, 0.5 delays for half the note duration, and 1 will wrap around to doing nothing again. The end result is a shuffle or swing-like rhythm

name: sysex
desc: MIDI sysex: Sends a MIDI sysex message.

name: sysexdata
desc: MIDI sysex data: Sends a MIDI sysex message.

name: sysexid
desc: MIDI sysex ID: Sends a MIDI sysex identifier message.

name: tables
desc: Loads a collection of wavetables to use with s

name: tag
desc: Tags each Hap with an identifier. Good for filtering. The function populates Hap.context.tags (Array).
ex:
s("saw!16").note("F1")
  .lpf(tri.range(40, 80).slow(4)).lpenv(5).lpq(4).lpd(0.15)
  .when(rand.late(0.1).gte(0.5), x => x.transpose("12").tag('altered'))
  .when(rand.late(0.2).gte(0.5), x => x.s("square").tag('altered'))
  .when("<0 1>", x => x.filter((hap) => hap.hasTag('altered')))

name: take
desc:
Experimental

Takes the given number of steps from a pattern (dropping the rest). A positive number will take steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.
ex:
"bd cp ht mt".take("2").sound()
// The same as "bd cp".sound()

"bd cp ht mt".take("1 2 3").sound()
// The same as "bd bd cp bd cp ht".sound()

"bd cp ht mt".take("-1 -2 -3").sound()
// The same as "mt ht mt cp ht mt".sound()

name: time
desc: A signal representing the cycle time.

name: timecat
desc: Aliases for stepcat

name: toBipolar
desc:
Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 ..

  1. Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the bipolar range -1 .. 1

name: tour
desc:
Experimental

Inserts a pattern into a list of patterns. On the first repetition it will be inserted at the end of the list, then moved backwards through the list on successive repetitions. The patterns are added together stepwise, with all repetitions taking place over a single cycle. Using pace to set the number of steps per cycle is therefore usually recommended.
ex:
"[c g]".tour("e f", "e f g", "g f e c").note()
   .sound("folkharp")
   .pace(8)

name: transient
desc: Transient shaper. Gives independent control over the emphasis on transients and sustains

name: transpose
desc:
Change the pitch of each value by the given amount. Expects numbers or note strings as values. The amount can be given as a number of semitones or as a string in interval short notation. If you don't care about enharmonic correctness, just use numbers. Otherwise, pass the interval of the form: ST where S is the degree number and T the type of interval with

  • M = major
  • m = minor
  • P = perfect
  • A = augmented
  • d = diminished

Examples intervals:

  • 1P = unison
  • 3M = major third
  • 3m = minor third
  • 4P = perfect fourth
  • 4A = augmented fourth
  • 5P = perfect fifth
  • 5d = diminished fifth

params.name: amount
params.desc: Either number of semitones or interval string.

name: tremolo
desc: Modulate the amplitude of a sound with a continuous waveform

name: tremolodepth
desc: Depth of amplitude modulation

name: tremolophase
desc: Alter the phase of the modulation waveform

params.name: offset
params.desc: the offset in cycles of the modulation

name: tremoloshape
desc: Shape of amplitude modulation
ex: note("{f g c d}%16").tremsync(4).tremoloshape("<sine tri square>").s("sawtooth")

name: tremoloskew
desc: Alter the shape of the modulation waveform

name: tremolosync
desc: Modulate the amplitude of a sound with a continuous waveform

name: tri
desc: A triangle signal between 0 and 1.

name: tri2
desc: A triangle signal between -1 and 1 (like tri, but bipolar).

name: undegrade
desc: Inverse of degrade: Randomly removes 50% of events from the pattern. Shorthand for .undegradeBy(0.5) Events that would be removed by degrade are let through by undegrade and vice versa (see second example).

name: undegradeBy
desc: Inverse of degradeBy: Randomly removes events from the pattern by a given amount. 0 = 100% chance of removal 1 = 0% chance of removal Events that would be removed by degradeBy are let through by undegradeBy and vice versa (see second example).

name: unison
desc: Set number of stacked voices for supported oscillators
ex: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").unison("<1 2 7>")

name: unit
desc: Used in conjunction with speed, accepts values of "r" (rate, default behavior), "c" (cycles), or "s" (seconds). Using unit "c" means speed will be interpreted in units of cycles, e.g. speed "1" means samples will be stretched to fill a cycle. Using unit "s" means the playback speed will be adjusted so that the duration is the number of seconds specified by speed.

name: useRNG
desc: Sets which random number generator to use. Historically Strudel would use useRNG('legacy'), which remains the default. To use a new more statistically precise RNG, try useRNG('precise').

name: velocity
desc: Sets the velocity from 0 to 1. Is multiplied together with gain.

name: vib
desc: Applies a vibrato to the frequency of the oscillator.
ex:
// change the modulation depth with ":"
note("a e")
.vib("<.5 1 2 4 8 16>:12")
._scope()

name: vibmod
desc: Sets the vibrato depth in semitones. Only has an effect if vibrato | vib | v is is also set
ex:
// change the vibrato frequency with ":"
note("a e")
.vibmod("<.25 .5 1 2 12>:8")
._scope()

name: voicing
desc:
Turns chord symbols into voicings. You can use the following control params:

  • chord: Note, followed by chord symbol, e.g. C Am G7 Bb^7
  • dict: voicing dictionary to use, falls back to default dictionary
  • anchor: the note that is used to align the chord
  • mode: how the voicing is aligned to the anchor
    • below: top note <= anchor
    • duck: top note <= anchor, anchor excluded
    • above: bottom note >= anchor
  • offset: whole number that shifts the voicing up or down to the next voicing
  • n: if set, the voicing is played like a scale. Overshooting numbers will be octaved

All of the above controls are optional, except chord. If you pass a pattern of strings to voicing, they will be interpreted as chords.

name: voicings
desc: DEPRECATED: still works, but it is recommended you use .voicing instead (without s). Turns chord symbols into voicings, using the smoothest voice leading possible. Uses chord-voicings package.
ex: stack("<C^7 A7 Dm7 G7>".voicings('lefthand'), "<C3 A2 D3 G2>").note()

name: vowel
desc: Formant filter to make things sound like vowels.

params.name: vowel
params.desc: You can use a e i o u ae aa oe ue y uh un en an on, corresponding to [a] [e] [i] [o] [u] [æ] [ɑ] [ø] [y] [ɯ] [ʌ] [œ̃] [ɛ̃] [ɑ̃] [ɔ̃]. Aliases: aa = å = ɑ, oe = ø = ö, y = ı, ae = æ.

ex: s("bd sd mt ht bd [~ cp] ht lt").vowel("[a|e|i|o|u]")

name: warp
desc: Amount of warp (alteration of the waveform) to apply to the wavetable oscillator

name: warpattack
desc: Attack time of the wavetable oscillator's warp envelope

name: warpdc
desc: DC offset of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

name: warpdecay
desc: Decay time of the wavetable oscillator's warp envelope

name: warpdepth
desc: Depth of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

name: warpenv
desc: Amount of envelope applied wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: warpmode
desc:
Type of warp (alteration of the waveform) to apply to the wavetable oscillator.

The current options are: none, asym, bendp, bendm, bendmp, sync, quant, fold, pwm, orbit, spin, chaos, primes, binary, brownian, reciprocal, wormhole, logistic, sigmoid, fractal, flip
ex:
s("morgana").bank("wt_digital").seg(8).note("F1").warp("0 0.25 0.5 0.75 1")
  .warpmode("<asym bendp spin logistic sync wormhole brownian>*2")

name: warprate
desc: Rate of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

name: warprelease
desc: Release time of the wavetable oscillator's warp envelope

name: warpshape
desc: Shape of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

name: warpskew
desc: Skew of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

params.name: skew
params.desc: How much to bend the LFO shape

name: warpsustain
desc: Sustain time of the wavetable oscillator's warp envelope

name: warpsync
desc: cycle synced rate of the LFO for the wavetable warp position

name: wchoose
desc: Chooses randomly from the given list of elements by giving a probability to each element

name: wchooseCycles
desc: Picks one of the elements at random each cycle by giving a probability to each element
ex: wchooseCycles(["c c c",5], ["a a a",3], ["f f f",1]).fast(4).note()

// The probability can itself be a pattern
wchooseCycles(["bd(3,8)","<5 0>"], ["hh hh hh",3]).fast(4).s()

name: when
desc: Applies the given function whenever the given pattern is in a true state.

name: whenKey
desc: Do something on a keypress, or array of keypresses Key name reference

name: within
desc: Use within to apply a function to only a part of a pattern.

params.name: func
params.desc: function to be applied to the sub-pattern

name: withSeed
desc: Modify a pattern by applying a function to the randomSeed control if present

params.name: func
params.desc: Function from seed (or undefined) to seed (or undefined)

name: wordfall
desc: Displays a vertical pianoroll with event labels. Supports all the same options as pianoroll.

name: wt
desc: Position in the wavetable of the wavetable oscillator

name: wtattack
desc: Attack time of the wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: wtdc
desc: DC offset of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

name: wtdecay
desc: Decay time of the wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: wtdepth
desc: Depth of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

name: wtenv
desc: Amount of envelope applied wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: wtphaserand
desc: Amount of randomness of the initial phase of the wavetable oscillator.

params.name: amount
params.desc: Randomness of the initial phase. Between 0 (not random) and 1 (fully random)

name: wtrate
desc: Rate of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

name: wtrelease
desc: Release time of the wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: wtshape
desc: Shape of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

name: wtskew
desc: Skew of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

params.name: skew
params.desc: How much to bend the LFO shape

name: wtsustain
desc: Sustain time of the wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: wtsync
desc: cycle synced rate of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

name: xfade
desc:
Cross-fades between left and right from 0 to 1:

  • 0 = (full left, no right)
  • .5 = (both equal)
  • 1 = (no left, full right)

name: zip
desc:
Experimental

'zips' together the steps of the provided patterns. This can create a long repetition, taking place over a single, dense cycle. Using pace to set the number of steps per cycle is therefore usually recommended.
ex:
zip("e f", "e f g", "g [f e] a f4 c").note()
   .sound("folkharp")
   .pace(8)

name: zoom
desc: Plays a portion of a pattern, specified by the beginning and end of a time span. The new resulting pattern is played over the time period of the original pattern:
ex:
s("bd*2 hh*3 [sd bd]*2 perc").zoom(0.25, 0.75)
// s("hh*3 [sd bd]*2") // equivalent
